name: Puzzle Difficulty Rater
description: Grades a puzzle by what solving it requires, not by how many givens it has. Clue count is a famously bad proxy — a 26-clue sudoku can be easier than a 30-clue one — so the rater solves the puzzle with a technique ladder and records the hardest technique it had to reach, plus how many times. That produces a grade that means the same thing across generated puzzles, which is what a difficulty selector needs in order not to be a lie. A puzzle the ladder cannot solve at all is reported as unrated rather than as hardest, because unsolvable-by-technique means it needs guessing and this genre does not ask players to guess.

inputs.name: techniqueLadder
inputs.description: Techniques in ascending difficulty. The hardest one required sets the grade.

inputs.name: gradeBands
inputs.description: Ladder index at which each named grade begins.

inputs.name: reportUnratedOnGuess
inputs.description: Whether a puzzle needing a guess is reported unrated rather than as hardest.

outputs.name: techniqueCounts
outputs.description: How often each technique was needed.
